extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, Scientific Review Officers, and NIH extramural staff involved in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria used in the NIH initial (SRG) and second-level (Advisory Council/Board) peer review of research grant and cooperative agreement applications, including scoring, review criteria, responsibilities, and post-review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The core values of peer review drive the NIH to seek the highest level of ethical standards: a process that strives to be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles form the foundation for laws, regulations, and policies governing NIH peer review and guide conduct of reviewers, SROs, and NIH staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOA-specified review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each FOA specifies all of the review criteria and considerations that will be used in the evaluation of applications submitted for that FOA; RFAs and certain Program Announcements may include additional review criteria and considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the FOA specifies otherwise, standard NIH review procedures and the NIH scoring system are followed. Different funding opportunity types (e.g., construction, fellowships) may use different criteria (see Review Criteria at a Glance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO is the NIH extramural staff scientist designated to ensure each application receives an objective and fair initial peer review and that applicable laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRO duties include analyzing application content and completeness, documenting and managing conflicts of interest, recruiting qualified reviewers, assigning applications to reviewers, overseeing administrative/regulatory aspects of meetings, and preparing summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are recruited based on scientific and technical qualifications and other considerations including authority in their scientific field, dedication to high quality fair and objective reviews, ability to work collegially in a group setting, experience in research grant review, and balanced representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs should recruit reviewers meeting these attributes to ensure expertise and collegial, fair review panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers must declare conflicts of interest, receive access to grant applications approximately six weeks prior to the meeting, maintain confidentiality, prepare a written critique using Review Critique Templates, assign numerical scores to each scored review criterion, and make recommendations on scientific/technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers also make recommendations concerning protections for human subjects, inclusion, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and appropriateness of budget requests; individual criterion scores and written critiques from assigned reviewers and discussants are reported to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and applicant conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must maintain the integrity of the peer review process by not contacting reviewers to influence the outcome, not sending information directly to a reviewer, and not accessing information related to the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are consequences for violating confidentiality or attempting to influence reviewers (see Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the review criteria and additional review criteria as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary overall impact scores are provided before meetings; discussed applications receive final impact scores from each eligible committee member which are averaged and multiplied by 10 to yield the final overall impact score (10 = high impact through 90 = low impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is one of the scored review criteria used to evaluate research grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers give a separate numerical score for Significance and include discussion in written critiques; the Significance score is considered when determining Overall Impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) is a scored review criterion assessing the qualifications, experience, and capacity of the project team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assign a numerical score to Investigator(s) and evaluate whether the investigators have the necessary skills to carry out the proposed work; this informs the Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is a scored review criterion that evaluates novel concepts, approaches, instrumentation, or methodologies proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers provide a numerical score and critique addressing the degree to which the project challenges existing paradigms or employs novel methods, informing the Overall Impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach is a scored review criterion evaluating the strategy, methodology, and analyses proposed to accomplish the aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers score Approach, assessing rigor, feasibility, potential pitfalls, and whether proposed methods are appropriate and well-reasoned; Approach score is a major component of Overall Impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment is a scored review criterion evaluating institutional support, resources, and collaborative environment that contribute to project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers score Environment based on facilities, institutional commitment, and whether the environment will meaningfully contribute to the probability of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections for Human Subjects will be evaluated as applicable for the project proposed; reviewers evaluate protections but do not give separate scores for these items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations of human subjects protections are used in determining scientific and technical merit and the Overall Impact score as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will evaluate plans for inclusion of women, minorities, and children, as applicable, though these items do not receive separate numeric scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion plans inform reviewers' judgment of scientific and technical merit and are reflected in the Overall Impact assessment where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and welfare of vertebrate animals in the proposed research will be evaluated as an additional review criterion (no separate numeric score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers make recommendations on vertebrate animal protections which factor into the Overall Impact determination when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biohazards associated with the proposed research will be evaluated as an additional review criterion, without separate numeric scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biohazard concerns inform reviewers' assessments of risk and feasibility and may affect Overall Impact considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission, Renewal, and Revision (additional review criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that are resubmissions, renewals, or revisions will have these statuses considered as additional review criteria (no separate numeric scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers take into account the application type (resubmission/renewal/revision) when evaluating merit and providing Overall Impact judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from foreign organizations are to be considered as applicable, but are an additional review consideration that should not receive separate scoring or be considered in providing Overall Impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This and other Additional Review Considerations (below) are evaluated but not scored and should not be used to determine the Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of select agents in the research is an additional review consideration and not a separately scored item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note select agent issues but should not give a separate score or include them in the Overall Impact calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource sharing plans (e.g., data, model organisms) are an additional review consideration and are not separately scored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may comment on resource sharing plans but should not assign separate numeric scores or factor them into Overall Impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication plans for key biological and/or chemical resources are an additional review consideration and are not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may evaluate whether authentication plans are adequate but should not score them separately or include them in Overall Impact scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and period of support are additional review considerations and should not be given separate scores or be considered in providing the Overall Impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may make recommendations concerning appropriateness of budget requests (see Budget Information for Reviewers), but budget should not drive the Overall Impact numeric score.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH scoring system (9-point scale and score calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for all applications; the same scale is used for overall impact and criterion scores. Final overall impact score is the mean of eligible members' final impact scores multiplied by 10, producing scores from 10 (high impact) to 90 (low impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before meetings, assigned reviewers give separate scores for each review criterion and a preliminary overall impact score. Preliminary scores often determine which applications will be discussed. Applications not discussed are marked ND and typically rank in the bottom half.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be designated NRFC by the SRG if it lacks significant and substantial merit; presents serious ethical problems in the protection of human subjects; or presents serious ethical problems in the use of vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRFC applications do not proceed to the second level of peer review (Advisory Council/Board) because they cannot be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement content and ND designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements provide written comments and scores from the assigned reviewers and discussants for each scored review criterion as feedback. Applications not discussed receive the designation ND (which may be reported as ++ on the face page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement will identify any percentiles and the base used to determine percentiles; applicants receiving summary statements should consult Next Steps guidance and may contact the program official for further advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile reporting and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile is the approximate percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year; percentiles are reported as whole numbers and only a subset of applications receive percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ad hoc study sections a different base may be used; the summary statement will identify the base used to determine the percentile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals grounds and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH peer review appeals are permitted if investigators believe the review process was flawed due to reviewer bias, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the review outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This appeals policy does not apply to appeals of technical evaluation of R&D contract projects, NIH funding decisions, or decisions concerning MERIT award extensions. See NOT-OD-11-064 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review considerations (Advisory Council/Board)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Councils/Boards and program staff examine applications and consider overall impact scores, percentile rankings (if applicable), summary statements, and the Institute/Center's priorities when making recommendations to the Institute/Center director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff provide a grant-funding plan to the Council; council members have access to applications and summary statements pending funding; Special Council Review applies for investigators receiving $1 million or more in direct costs to consider additional funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review funding decision process and paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: After peer review, IC program staff use impact scores, percentiles, summary statements, and IC priorities to inform funding strategies; some ICs publish paylines to guide applicants on likelihood of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with fundable scores should consult program officials for guidance; if awarded, applicants work with program officials and Grants Management Officers to prepare awards. Paylines are fiscal-year-specific and may be delayed at the start of fiscal years.
